name: Plitvice and Istria, Croatia
summary: Waterfalls in a forest, then a slower peninsula. April is the waterfall month. It is not the month for island-hopping.
why: Plitvice in April has water and fewer people than July. Istria adds hill towns and a coast without asking the group to live on ferries. One country, two bases, a sensible fortnight.
distinctive: A chain of lakes pouring into each other on wooden walks, close to a peninsula of small towns that is calmer than Dubrovnik.
weather: Plitvice sits up in the forest and is cooler than the coast. A travel model of April there cited about 14°C by day and 6°C at night, with frequent rain. Istria is milder. The sea is not warm. Seasonal, not a forecast.
crowds: Park writers describe April as low to moderate, with a bump if your dates hit Easter week. Easter 2027 is 28 March, so mid-April should be past that bump. Timed tickets are now part of the park's crowd management. Summer is the packed season.
natureExperiences: Plitvice's lower lakes and one waterfall route, not every boardwalk
Istrian hill lanes and an olive grove
A coast walk in Rovinj or Poreč
age6: The boat and the easier boardwalks. Wooden paths get slippery. Hold hands. Leave before they are tired, even if you have paid for a long route.
age12: The lake system as a water cycle you can see, plus a fort or a hill town.
age14: The same, and the question of why the park now uses timed entry.
adults: The water, the food in Istria, and Roman Parentium in Poreč if you want one serious building.
gettingAround: A car, or two. Croatia drives on the right. Ferries to Hvar or Korčula are the wrong tool in April. Many island services are still thin.
meetingPoint: Zagreb is the straightforward airport, then a drive south to the lakes. Both families connect through Europe. Venice or Ljubljana are possible alternates and add a border.
visaAu: Croatia is Schengen. Australian passports are visa-free for a short stay. EES applies. ETIAS was not operating.
visaIn: Indian passports need a Schengen visa. Apply to Croatia if the nights are mostly there.
disadvantages: The boardwalks are the attraction and the fatigue. Do not plan two full route days back to back for age 6.
April is a poor month for the Dalmatian islands. This plan stays north on purpose.
Plitvice is famous. Timed entry and an early start are how you keep it pleasant.
uncertainties: 2027 ticket windows and which routes are open.
Rain. The park is wet even in a good April.
Ferry fantasies. Recheck Jadrolinija before adding any island.

gain: The best waterfall landscape that still fits a calm April pace.
miss: A city-and-science balance, and any swimming holiday.
stretch16: Add free days in Istria. Do not add Dubrovnik and Split.

days.experience: Land and walk the upper town only if you are awake.
days.optional: A playground or a cake shop
days.highlight: A compact capital used as a landing
days.transfer: Long-haul connections into Zagreb. Airport bus or taxi.
days.seasonal: April is cool in the city.

days.experience: Drive to the lakes and do not enter the park yet.
days.optional: A short look from a roadside view if one is safe
days.kids: Car day. About 2 hours from Zagreb in normal traffic.
days.transfer: About 2 hours. Stay in the park villages, not back in Zagreb.
days.seasonal: Book the timed entry for tomorrow morning before you leave home.

days.experience: One route, early. Use the boat. Stop when the 6-year-old stops.
days.optional: A second waterfall only if everyone is still cheerful
days.kids: Slippery boards. Shoes with grip. A snack before someone crashes.
days.transfer: Inside the park, on foot and by the park boat or shuttle.
days.seasonal: April water is a reason people who know the park like this month. Rain gear belongs in the daypack.
days.wet: Go anyway unless it is a storm. The falls are better with water. Cut the route short.

days.experience: A shorter second entry, or a full rest day if yesterday was enough.
days.seasonal: One great park day beats two tired ones.

days.experience: Drive west to Rovinj or Poreč and stay.
days.highlight: The Adriatic at a walking pace
days.kids: Ice cream. The sea is cold.
days.transfer: About 3–4 hours from Plitvice to Istria. This is the long drive. Stop for lunch.
days.seasonal: Island ferries are not the plan.
days.wet: The old town is sheltered enough for a wander.

days.experience: The old town slowly. One church or the Euphrasian basilica in Poreč if you are based nearby.
days.optional: A boat ride in the bay, not an island
days.highlight: Venetian lanes and a serious early-Christian mosaic, in a small dose
days.kids: Lanes for age 6. Mosaics for ages 12 and 14, for half an hour.
days.seasonal: Some seasonal restaurants are shut. The town is not.
days.wet: The basilica or a museum, then a long lunch.

days.experience: A hill town such as Motovun or Grožnjan.
days.highlight: Inland Istria, which is quieter than the coast
days.kids: A short uphill. Truffles are a smell and a story. Skip a long tasting.
days.transfer: Under an hour from the coast towns.
days.seasonal: April is green in the hills.

days.experience: A free beach-walk day. No swimming plan.
days.optional: Bikes on a flat prom if the rental has a child option
days.wet: A cooking class or a rainy-day aquarium if one is open nearby. Confirm before you promise it.

days.experience: A second hill or a cape, then a free afternoon.
days.optional: Rt Kamenjak only if the wind is kind and the walk is short
days.highlight: A wilder edge of the peninsula
days.kids: Keep it short. The cliffs are not a playground.
days.transfer: South of the main towns. Allow the drive.

days.experience: Fly from Pula if seven seats exist. Otherwise drive back to Zagreb and fly the next morning with a buffer night.
days.transfer: Pula's international schedule is thinner than Zagreb's. Confirm 2027 before you plan the last night there.
days.seasonal: A buffer night in Zagreb is the safer pattern.
